headline: Blowout payrolls lift 2-year yield 5bp and knock gold 0.9%; oil steadies after a 13% weekly slide
summary: A 165,000 October payrolls beat pushed December Fed hike odds to about 70–77% and lifted the 2-year about 5bp to near 4.52%, flattening the curve, while gold fell back to $4,064.50 as yields and the dollar firmed. Oil was flat on the day, WTI +0.3% at $90.83, but posted its biggest weekly loss since 2022 on US–Iran de-escalation hopes. European bonds hit multi-month lows in the morning tech rout, then gave the gains back after the US data.
drivers: Jobs beat revives December hike pricing

Payrolls rose 165,000 vs about 65,000 expected, with 84,000 of upward revisions, unemployment at 4.1% and wages +0.4% m/m. The 2-year rose about 5bp to 4.52%, the 10-year about 2bp to 4.86%, and 2s10s flattened to about 33bp.
Oil stalls as US–Iran talk offsets tanker attacks

Reports that Washington and Tehran are closer to a deal capped prices even as attacks on ships near Hormuz continued. WTI settled +$0.31 at $90.83 and Brent +$0.03 at $98.32, leaving WTI down 12.8% on the week.
Firmer yields and dollar trim gold's best week since August

Comex gold settled -$38 at $4,064.50 and silver -43¢ at $51.80 as hike odds rose and the dollar index hit a one-week high near 102. Both still gained about 5% on the week; Goldman cut its end-2026 gold target to $4,150.
Bunds touched 3.21% and Schatz 2.92%, the lowest since late August, as the tech rout spread, but the US data pushed yields back to near 3.25% and 3.00%. OATs held near 4.77%, about 152bp over Bunds.

oil.note: Dec WTI settled +$0.31 (+0.3%) at $90.83, down 12.8% on the week; Jan Brent +$0.03 at $98.32.
oil.why: Two forces cancelled out. Fresh attacks on ships near Hormuz and Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries lifted Brent briefly above $100 overnight, but a report that the US and Iran are nearing a breakthrough, with Tehran more flexible on its nuclear programme, pulled prices back. Tech-led de-risking also hit commodity positions, so WTI ended barely higher after a $19 weekly range and its biggest weekly drop since 2022.
oil.outlook: Expect a choppy $86–95 range with headline risk both ways: deal hopes cap rallies, while Iran's demands (lifting the blockade and sanctions) and ongoing ship attacks keep a premium in. A close above $94 points to renewed escalation; a confirmed deal could break $86.
oil.watch: US–Iran headlines, EIA STEO Tue Nov 10, OPEC report Wed Nov 11, EIA stocks Thu Nov 12 and the IEA report Fri Nov 13.

gas.note: Dec RBOB rose 1.33¢ (+0.5%) to $2.7767, still down 12% on the week, the biggest weekly drop since 2020.
gas.why: Gasoline edged up with crude on Friday but the week's story is the collapse of the war premium: RBOB lost about 38¢ as US–Iran deal hopes and the midterm result knocked crude down 13%. Winter-grade blends and softer post-season demand add to the weakness, and diesel underperformed on the day, with ULSD down 0.5% to $4.33. The AAA pump average started Friday near $4.07, about 14¢ lower than a week earlier.
gas.outlook: Bias sideways to lower in a $2.65–2.90 range as pump prices catch down to futures and could fall below $4 next week for the first time since mid-July. Only a crude spike back above $94 WTI would lift RBOB toward $3.
gas.watch: Crude and Iran headlines, EIA gasoline stocks and refinery runs Thu Nov 12, and the AAA average breaking $4.

gold.note: Comex Nov settled -$38.00 (-0.9%) at $4,064.50, still +4.6% on the week; spot near $4,066.
gold.why: Gold gave back Thursday's gain as the 165,000 payrolls beat, 4.1% unemployment and 0.4% wage growth lifted December Fed hike odds to roughly 70–77% and pushed the 2-year yield up about 5bp. The dollar index hit a one-week high near 102 and the tech rebound cut haven demand. Goldman Sachs also cut its end-2026 target to $4,150 from $4,650, citing the Fed's hawkish turn.
gold.outlook: Range of $4,000–4,150 with a slight downside tilt while hike odds stay high; support sits at $4,035 and $4,000, resistance at $4,100–4,146. A soft CPI on Tuesday that pulls hike odds below 60% would reopen $4,150–4,200.
gold.watch: US CPI Tue Nov 10, PPI Fri Nov 13, Fed speakers including Bowman and Goolsbee Mon Nov 9, and the dollar.

silver.note: Comex Nov settled -43¢ (-0.8%) at $51.80, still +5.5% on the week, the best week since August.
silver.why: Silver followed gold lower as stronger US jobs data lifted Fed hike odds, real yields and the dollar. The rebound in chip stocks helped its industrial story at the margin, so it fell slightly less than gold in percentage terms, and the gold/silver ratio held near 78–79. Profit-taking after a 5% jump on Wednesday added to the dip.
silver.outlook: Range of about $50–54 with a mild downside tilt while the Fed looks set to hike; a close below $49 would retest the October low. A tech recovery plus a soft CPI is what it needs to break above $54.
silver.watch: US CPI Nov 10, chip-stock sentiment and China trade and inflation data.

us2y.note: Up about 5bp to near 4.52% after the payrolls beat, though still a sixth straight weekly fall.
us2y.why: The 2-year is the most Fed-sensitive point, and the October jobs report was strong on every line: 165,000 jobs vs about 65,000 expected, 84,000 of upward revisions, 4.1% unemployment and 0.4% wage growth. Futures moved December hike odds to about 70–77% from near 67%, and Michigan sentiment beat at 51. It touched 4.54% before the tech rebound and haven unwind steadied it.
us2y.outlook: Bias modestly higher in a 4.45–4.62% range while a December hike looks likely; the front end now hinges on CPI. A soft core print would send it back toward 4.45%, while a hot one opens 4.60%.
us2y.watch: 3-year auction Mon Nov 9, CPI Tue Nov 10, PPI Fri Nov 13 and Fed speakers before the Dec 9 meeting.

us5y.note: Up about 4bp to near 4.65%, giving back part of the week's haven rally.
us5y.why: The belly rose almost as much as the 2-year because the jobs beat put more 2027 tightening back into the price: futures again show at least 40bp of hikes by September 2027. Lower oil earlier in the week had pushed 5-year breakevens down to about 2.27% from 2.5%, which limited the selloff, as did investors who had said they would buy a post-payrolls dip.
us5y.outlook: Range of 4.55–4.72% with a slight upward bias into CPI and refunding supply; 4.72% is the level that would show the week's rally has fully unwound. A soft CPI points back to 4.55%.
us5y.watch: 3-year auction Nov 9, CPI Nov 10 and the 10-year auction Nov 10.

us10y.note: Up about 2bp to near 4.86% after touching 4.90%; 2s10s flattened to about 33bp from 37bp.
us10y.why: The jobs beat pushed the 10-year up as much as 6bp to about 4.90%, but buyers returned as it faded: investors positioned to add duration on a dip, oil stayed below $91, and the overseas haven bid from the tech rout was still around. Because the move was about Fed hikes, the curve bear-flattened, with the 2-year rising twice as much as the 10-year.
us10y.outlook: Range of 4.78–4.95% with a flat bias; refunding supply ($42bn of 10s on Tuesday) and hike pricing cap rallies, while lower oil limits selloffs. A hot CPI would test 4.95%; a soft one with weak demand for risk would bring 4.78% back.
us10y.watch: CPI and the 10-year auction Tue Nov 10, bond market closed Wed Nov 11 for Veterans Day.

us30y.note: Up about 1–2bp to near 5.27%, the smallest rise on the curve as it flattened.
us30y.why: Long bonds rose least because a Fed that hikes into strong data is seen as protecting long-run inflation control, which flattens the curve. Breakevens near multi-week lows after the oil slump also helped. Still, investors are holding back ahead of next week's $25bn 30-year auction, which kept the long end from rallying with the morning haven bid.
us30y.outlook: Range of 5.18–5.35% with a flattening bias while hike pricing builds; a weak 30-year auction or an oil rebound would test 5.35%.
us30y.watch: CPI Nov 10 and the 30-year auction Thu Nov 12.

de2y.note: Reversed up to near 3.00% after touching 2.92%, the lowest since late August.
de2y.why: Schatz yields fell early as the global tech rout drove money into safe bonds, then turned higher once US payrolls lifted Fed hike odds and Treasury yields. ECB pricing stays firm: euro-area inflation is at 4.0%, the deposit rate is 2.5%, and Lagarde said on Thursday that incoming data will decide whether a December hike is needed, with several governors already leaning toward one.
de2y.outlook: Range of 2.90–3.05% with a December ECB hike largely priced; a sustained Brent drop below $90 would be needed to unwind it. Bias flat.
de2y.watch: Eurogroup Mon Nov 9, German final CPI Wed Nov 11, euro-area Q3 GDP Fri Nov 13 and the ECB Dec 17.

de5y.note: Little changed near 3.05% after dipping in the morning haven rush.
de5y.why: The 5-year swung with Treasuries: the tech rout and lower oil drove an early rally, and the US jobs beat erased it. ECB hike expectations, built on 4.0% euro-area inflation, kept a floor under yields even at the low, so the belly ended the week only modestly lower than it started.
de5y.outlook: Range of 2.95–3.12% with no strong bias; a hot US CPI or Brent back above $100 would push it toward 3.12%.
de5y.watch: US CPI Nov 10, German CPI Nov 11 and euro-area GDP Nov 13.

de10y.note: Little changed near 3.25% after touching 3.21%, the lowest since late August; a fourth straight weekly fall.
de10y.why: Bunds hit a two-and-a-half-month low in the morning as the tech selloff spread to Europe and Japan, shrugging off Brent near $99. The rally reversed after the US payrolls beat sent Treasury yields higher, leaving the 10-year roughly where it started. Over the week, lower oil and haven demand pulled it down about 9bp from 3.34%.
de10y.outlook: Range of 3.18–3.32% with a slight downward bias while equities stay fragile; a Brent move back above $100 or hawkish ECB talk would send it toward 3.32%. Fitch's review of Germany on Nov 13 is unlikely to move it.
de10y.watch: US CPI Nov 10, German CPI Nov 11, euro-area GDP Nov 13 and the ECB Dec 17.

de30y.note: Little changed near 3.64% after touching 3.61%, the lowest since end-July.
de30y.why: The long end joined the morning haven rally, reaching its lowest since July, then gave it back as the US jobs data lifted global yields. Heavy German issuance to fund fiscal expansion keeps investors demanding a premium, so the 30-year has lagged the 10-year in the rally and the curve stays steep.
de30y.outlook: Range of 3.58–3.72% with a steepening bias; a break above 3.72% would need an oil spike or a hawkish ECB shift.
de30y.watch: German auctions, US CPI Nov 10 and global long-end supply including the US 30-year Nov 12.

fr2y.note: Edged up to near 3.55% as US data lifted short rates after the morning rally faded.
fr2y.why: Short OATs follow ECB pricing, and the strong US jobs report nudged global front-end yields higher after the morning haven bid. December ECB hike expectations, with euro-area inflation at 4.0%, stay the anchor. French politics weighs less on the 2-year than on longer maturities, though the budget rejection and Thursday's strike keep investors cautious.
fr2y.outlook: Range of 3.45–3.60%; the front end mostly follows the ECB, so a dovish turn after a lasting oil drop is the main downside trigger. Bias flat.
fr2y.watch: French Q3 unemployment Tue Nov 10, French final CPI Fri Nov 13 and the ECB Dec 17.

fr5y.note: Little changed near 4.14%, holding the week's gains as the morning rally and US data offset.
fr5y.why: The 5-year OAT moved with Bunds and ended flat. Lower oil helped French debt more than German this week because energy feeds directly into France's fiscal and growth outlook, but the Assembly's rejection of the 2027 budget's first part keeps a risk premium in. The government's bill now goes to the Senate, with a vote set for Dec 9.
fr5y.outlook: Range of 4.05–4.22% with spread risk skewed wider into the Senate process; a clear path to a 2027 budget would bring 4.05% into play.
fr5y.watch: Senate budget debate, French CPI Nov 13 and S&P's Italy and Fitch's Germany reviews Nov 13 for read-across.

fr10y.note: Little changed near 4.77%; the spread to Bunds held near 152bp, well below the late-October peak near 175bp.
fr10y.why: OATs gained about 1bp in the morning with Bunds and then gave it back after US payrolls, so the spread was steady. The spread has tightened sharply over two weeks as lower oil eased deficit fears, but investors stopped chasing it after Wednesday's unanimous rejection of the budget's first part and Thursday's strike. ING sees about 150bp as a floor while political risk lasts.
fr10y.outlook: Range of 4.68–4.88%, with the spread likely held at 145–160bp; a budget passed even by decree could tighten it toward 140bp, while a government crisis would send it back above 160bp.
fr10y.watch: Senate budget debate, the Dec 9 Senate vote and rating reviews.

fr30y.note: Little changed near 5.32%, still close to its highs as fiscal risk kept the long end heavy.
fr30y.why: The 30-year OAT barely moved as the morning haven rally and the post-payrolls rise in global yields cancelled out. Long-dated French debt carries the most fiscal and political risk, with deficits near 5% of GDP and debt heading toward 122% of GDP in 2027, so it has lagged the rally in shorter OATs.
fr30y.outlook: Range of 5.22–5.42% with a bias to underperform shorter OATs; a credible budget deal could pull it toward 5.20%, while political escalation risks a retest of the highs.
fr30y.watch: French politics, Senate budget debate and OAT auctions.
